text.p: SME - Jan Luptak, leader of the minor coalition partner, the ultra-left Workers Party (ZRS), said ZRS would again vote in favour of postponing bank privatisation, even if Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar decides to connect the vote on the law barring the sell-off with a no-confidence vote against his government.
- Luptak, however, said his party does not support attempts to call early elections.

- Jozef Migas, chairman of the opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL), said there were other ways to solve the current crisis inside the ruling coalition than calling early elections. Migas suggested a non-political government of experts, minority government or creating a new coalition with majority government.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovakia's largest commercial bank VUB a.s. said it had expected parliament to approve the law postponing the bank privatisation, saying there was no need to hurry with such move.

- VUB President Jan Gabriel said the foreign strategic investor should be allowed to take a stake in privatisation of VUB, as he considers domestic capital sources inadequate fully to privatise the bank.

- Heavy-engineering company ZTS Dubnica expects losses of about 331 million crowns in 1996, some 1.1 billion crowns less than losses in 1995. ZTS said it planned to increase production by some 900 million crowns in 1997 from last year's 1.26 billion crowns.
NARODNA OBRODA - President Michal Kovac has won a law suit against the pro-governmental daily Slovenska Republika, which last year accused him of having an illegal account in a foreign bank.

- The state social insurance company said it would propose a 10 percent increase in pensions, effective from July this year. The planned increase should be covered from the insurer's surpluses in 1996 and 1997.
- Slovakia's fourth largest commercial bank Polnobanka extended around 1.734 billion crowns in loans for the agricultural sector last year.
PRAVDA - The International Law Court in Hague will start law suit between Slovakia and Hungary over the controversial Gabcikovo dam on river Danube on March 3.
- The French-Slovak chemical joint venture Chemlon Humenne, producing mainly polyamide fibres, plans to invest about 350 million crowns in modernisation projects this year.
